key_idea: Show that a homogenized generating polynomial of independent sets (a degeneration of the Potts model partition function) is Lorentzian; setting all matroid variables equal then gives a bivariate Lorentzian polynomial, and for bivariate polynomials being Lorentzian is the same as having ultra log-concave coefficients.
reason: Within the excerpt the proof takes three lines: it chains a limit, the fact that Lorentzian polynomials are preserved under nonnegative linear changes of variables, and the bivariate characterization, so the ultra log-concavity follows from a structural property and not from a computation. The real work sits in the general Lorentzian theory and in Theorem 72, so the result is elegant as a payoff of that framework, not as a standalone book proof.
recognized: Brändén–Huh, 'Lorentzian polynomials' (Annals 2020), proof of Mason's strongest conjecture (Theorem 4.14)
